tarif: Tetracyclic triterpenes named after dammar resin, a natural resin first isolated from tropical trees of the DIPTEROCARPACEAE family.
A second-generation cephalosporin antibacterial agent. Cefprozil has a phenyl ring at the C-3 position of its cephalosporin core.
A 58 kDa membrane protein and delta(14)-sterol reductase that is found in the NUCLEAR ENVELOPE. Deficiencies of this receptor cause PELGER-HUET ANOMALY.

Frogs that sequester and secrete POISONS (e.g., BATRACHOTOXINS). Poison frogs include Australian Pseudophryne, Central and South American Dendrobates, Epipedobates, and Phyllobates and Madagascan Mantella. Melanophyrniscus is a poison toad in the family of Bufonidae. All poison dart frogs are from rain forest of western Colombia and are members of Phyllobates.

Protein complex constituents that bind chromosomes from late G1 until the metaphase - anaphase transition. The cohesin complex regulates sister chromatid cohesion, HOMOLOGOUS RECOMBINATION and DNA looping.
Signaling proteins that are synthesized and released by muscle fibers in response to exercise or other forms of physical activity.
A time mismatch between patient's inspiratory effort and MECHANICAL VENTILATOR's inspiratory time.

An annual species in the family ASTERACEA, genus Parthenium which sometimes is referred to as feverfew, not to be confused with the medicinal herb often cultivated in the garden, TANACETUM PARTHENIUM. Parthenium hysterophorus is an invasive allelopathic weed indigenous to the Caribbean, Central and South America and has similar rosette stage structures as COMMON RAGWEED. It contains sesquiterpene lactones including parthenin which is poisonous to grazing animals and allergenic and irritant, causing Parthenium dermatitis in humans.
Family of enzymes that catalyze the formation of GalNAcAlpha1-serine/threonine linkages in glycoproteins.
A transcriptional repressor in the ETS transcription factor family. Contains a unique ETS domain and HLH domain that can interfere with protein-protein interactions.

A non-intensive, reversible medical intervention achieved by using compounds that mimic the actions of GONADOTROPIN-RELEASING HORMONE (GnRH), which in turn slows or stops the physical changes associated with puberty such as the development of breasts or facial hair.
A small rac GTP-binding protein that forms one of the components of the NADPH oxidase enzyme system.
A MAP kinase kinase kinase that activates the SAPK/JNK and p38/ERK SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION pathways. It has multiple interaction domains, including a Cdc42 binding motif.
A retinoic acid receptor that regulates transcriptional activity by heterodimerizing with nuclear RETINOID X RECEPTORS.
Agents that are used to temporarily suppress puberty in adolescents.
A protein serine-threonine kinase that catalyzes the activation of canonical and non-canonical NF-kappaB pathways.
giris_terimleri: Mitogen Activated Protein Kinase Kinase Kinase 14

tarif: Non-traditional journal impact measures that include tracking of downloads; mentions in SOCIAL MEDIA, NEWS reports, BLOGS, and online ENCYCLOPEDIAS; links in bookmarking services and online reference managers; and crowd-based reviews.

Various cellular responses cells undergo in order to sustain energy production under cellular METABOLIC STRESS. Oncogenic metabolic reprogramming is one of the hallmarks of cancer progression and metastasis.
The use of various imaging and image enhancement techniques in forensic investigative disciplines. It often includes FORENSIC MEDICINE platforms such as X-RAYS; CT XRAY; and MRI.

Computing that deals with approximate models and gives solutions to complex real-life problems. Has greater tolerance for imprecision, uncertainty, partial truth, and approximations. Based on techniques such as FUZZY LOGIC, genetic algorithms, NEURAL NETWORKS, COMPUTER, MACHINE LEARNING, and EXPERT SYSTEMS.
The state of being imprisoned or confined.
The environment concerned with the pursuit of research, education, and scholarship.
Compounds that stimulate the activity of GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 RECEPTOR. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists are used to treat TYPE 2 DIABETES and OBESITY.

Enzymes that are produced and secreted by organisms, including bacterial and fungi.They are involved in a variety of biological processes, such as nutrient acquisition, pathogenesis of candida, and host tissue invasion.

Minimal elements within a protein that are sufficient for recognition and degradation by a proteolytic apparatus. Inherent degrons are comprised of short linear amino acid sequences and secondary protein structural features that increase the affinity to E3 LIGASE; and are involved in regulating the specificity and timing of PROTEIN DEGRADATION. Acquired degrons are mostly transient and conferred by post-translational modifications of specific amino acids within proteins. (From Mol Cell. 2016 Sep 15;63(6):1055-65)
An inhibitor of matrix metalloproteinases involved in regulation of PLATELET AGGREGATION and recruitment.
CASEIN-like globular storage proteins from leguminous seeds such as peas.
An epithelium-specific basement membrane adhesion molecule that is a component of anchoring filaments. Consists of 3 subunits (A, B2, & B1).
CA(2+) MG(2+)-ATPASE inhibitor found in membranes of mammalian ERYTHROCYTES.
Phosphoprotein found in nucleoli, on the cell membrane, and in cytoplasm of all higher eukaryotes. They act as a receptor for some viruses, bacteria, and toxins.
Active compound in herbicidal formulations that inhibits 3-PHOSPHOSHIKIMATE 1-CARBOXYVINYLTRANSFERASE.

Reductions in edible FOOD post-harvesting anywhere along the food supply chain, e.g., due to spoilage, improper storage, excessive food preparation, resulting in REFUSE DISPOSAL of potentially useful food mass.

A glycoprotein member of the immunoglobulin superfamily that is primarily expressed on the surface of DENDRITIC CELLS. It is believed to play a role in ANTIGEN PRESENTATION and CELL-TO-CELL INTERACTION following LYMPHOCYTE ACTIVATION.

A transitory embryonic structure that appears during the 5th week post-fertilization. The ganglionic eminence plays an important in the development of the nervous system by guiding tangential cell and axon migration during embryonic development and give rise to BASAL GANGLIA and cortical GABAergic and thalamic and olfactory INTERNEURONS.
A 220 kDa non-fibrillar collagen and basement membrane component. It is involved in healing wounds of the EPITHELIUM, CORNEAL.
A high-affinity KAINATE and GLUTAMATE receptor that functions as ligand-gated ion channel in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSYEM and plays an essential role in NEURONAL PLASTICITY.
A medical procedure in which medication is delivered directly into the ANTERIOR CHAMBER of the eye.
A high-affinity KAINATE and GLUTAMATE receptor that functions as ligand-gated ion channel in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSYEM and modulates excitatory synaptic transmission.

A zinc dependent transcription factor involved in the regulation of intracellular signaling pathways. Regulates the expression of two streams of genes functioning in metal homeostasis and anti-oxidative response.
Membrane-bound proteins found in the ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM of CULTURED CELLS and NEOPLASMS. They were identified originally based on their capacity to bind THYROID HORMONE.
Transmembrane enzymes of the Golgi network that recognize glycans attached to LIPIDS and PROTEINS passing through the secretory pathway.
A process of actively learning and adapting to new ways to function following a challenging life crisis.
Various techniques for actively managing a stressful event or situation.
The extent to which job separations are involuntary. The primary measure of job security is the rate of job loss (https://www.bls.gov/osmr/research-papers/2002/pdf/ec020050.pdf).
A state of feeling emotionally overextended and drained.
The extent to which individuals encounter messages and content via COMMUNICATION MEDIA.
A state of tension or distress that occurs when fulfilling roles of one status making it difficult to fulfill the roles of another.

Failure to seek timely and appropriate care or allow such care for medical, dental or psychological needs by family members, legal guardian and other caregivers. Negligence by professionals is PROFESSIONAL NEGLIGENCE.

Synthetic biopolymers that are formed by repeating amino acid sequences that are naturally found in TROPOELASTIN. They are useful for various purposes, including DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEMS, TISSUE SCAFFOLDS, and ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS.
Field of genetics studying correlates between variations in SOCIOLOGICAL FACTORS and differences in GENOME-wide GENE EXPRESSION REGULATION.
Structurally related ALKALOIDS derived from the plants of the monocotyledonous family STEMONACEAE, characterized by the presence of a pyrrolo(1,2-a)azepine or a pyrido(1,2-a)azepine nucleus.
Perceptions of PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS based on the individual's own personal values, beliefs and past and current experiences and circumstances.
A group of proteins that control the activity of PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES.
Sesquiterpene compounds that contain an INDOLE.

A biomedical database and research resource that contains genetic and health data on participants aged 40-69 years with a roughly even number of men and women recruited between 2006 and 2010 throughout the UK.

Differentiated trophoblast cells originally from trophoblastic cell columns of anchoring CHORIONIC VILLI of the DECIDUA basalis of the PLACENTA. Extravillous trophoblasts invade into the uterine structures, attaching the placenta to the UTERUS. They are also found in chorionic plate, MYOMETRIUM, and spiral arteries.

A series of thickened ECTODERM patches in the developing cranial region that appears during week 4 in human embryo. Ectodermal placodes are the primordium of many ectodermal sensory systems including the INNER EAR, the EYE LENS, the OLFACTORY EPITHELIUM, as well as the PITUITARY GLAND and THYROID GLAND.

Remedial treatment or preventive procedures of a disease which is done too infrequently or not enough to control disease diagnosis or treatment. Many factors contribute to medical undertreatment including lack of ACCESS TO HEALTH SERVICES and PATIENT PREFERENCE.
Anesthesia method that deals with the complexities of the physiology and pharmacology of the nervous system when providing anesthesia for patients undergoing neurological procedures.

Protein serine-threonine kinases which regulate entry into M phase, spindle pole biogenesis and function, mitotic chromosome dynamics, mitotic exit, and cytokinesis. They contain a characteristic Polo-box protein interaction domain.
Plays a crucial role in the regulation of proliferative activity of normal and malignant cells. Proposed as a new target for antineoplastic treatment strategies.
Conducting anesthesia procedures in AGED adults, typically those aged 65 years and older.
A mitochondrion and plasma membrane protein that enables choline transmembrane transporter activity.
Conducting anesthesia procedures in infants, children, and adolescents.
The generation of images of the body's structures, organs, and tissues after death.

Bactericidal agents that contain a beta-lactam ring in their chemical structure. They inhibit bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to PENICILLIN-BINDING PROTEINS, preventing the synthesis of peptidoglycan in bacterial cell walls.
Ligand-gated cation-selective ION CHANNELS located in ENDOSOMES and LYSOSOMES of plant and animal cells.

CEPHALOSPORIN agents with excellent coverage against gram-positive cocci, such as STAPHYLOCOCCUS  and STREPTOCOCCUS. They have some activity against the gram-negative bacteria, but in general, gram-negative activity is decreased compared to 2nd, 3rd, and 4th generation cephalosporins.
A family of single-pass transmembrane receptors that act as the cognate receptors for the secreted guidance factor Slit emanating from central nervous system midlines.
The addition of a methyl group to one of the NITROGEN atoms on a NUCLEOTIDE base in an RNA molecule.

The flow of SEMINAL FLUID, from the posterior URETHRA, backwards into the BLADDER. Causes include injuries such as from SPINAL CORD INJURIES; DIABETIC NEUROPATHIES; surgeries in adjacent tissues such as AORTIC ANEURYSM surgeries and transurethral bladder neck incisions; or drug side effects.
Agents with less activity against gram-positive cocci than FIRST GENERATION CEPHALOSPORINS but have increased activity against gram-negative bacilli.
The inability in males to ejaculate, or to have a normal time to EJACULATION.

Agents that are structurally similar to other CEPHALOSPORINS but have a broader spectrum of activity against bacteria than the first and second generation cephalosporins. These agents cover more resistant STREPTOCOCCUS, STAPHYLOCOCCUS, gram-positive anaerobes, and more resistant strains of HAEMOPHILUS, NEISSERIA, PROTEUS, ESCHERICHIA COLI, and KLEBSIELLA (HNPEK).
Agents that stimulate TOLL-LIKE RECEPTOR signaling, and the activity of both the INNATE IMMUNE RESPONSE and ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY.
Contrast imaging generated from the measurements of phase shift changes of light waves as they pass through transparent objects of varying thickness and refractivity.
A microanalytical technique combining mass spectrometry and liquid chromatography for the qualitative as well as quantitative determinations of compounds.

A supportive healthcare, consisting of medical, surgical, mental health, and non-medical services for TRANSGENDER PERSONS and GENDER-NONCONFORMING PERSONS. Medical and psychosocial gender affirming healthcare practices may lower rates of adverse mental health outcomes, build SELF ESTEEM, and improve overall QUALITY OF LIFE for transgender and gender diverse youth (https://opa.hhs.gov/sites/default/files/2022-03/gender-affirming-care-young-people-march-2022.pdf).
An orphan nuclear receptor that belongs to the ERR subfamily. It has enriched expression in tissues with high oxidative metabolic capacity.
Sense of time urgency to complete a task. This sense of time urgency creates psychological pressure affecting performance (https://www.nrc.gov/docs/ML2112/ML21127A272.pdf).

A version of the game of baggataway, in which two teams of players use long-handled, racketlike implements (crosses) to catch, carry, or throw a ball down the field or into the opponents’ goal. The goal is defined by uprights and a crossbar framing a loose net. The distinctive feature of the game is the crosse (lacrosse stick), the implement used by the players to carry, catch, and pass the ball. The crosse is sharply bent at the top to form a hook from the end of which a thong is drawn and fastened to the shaft about 2 or 3 feet from the end of the handle, forming an oval triangle that is woven with a loose network of leather, nylon, or gut to form the pocket with which the ball is handled.(from https://www.britannica.com/sports/lacrosse)

The design, development and management of sustainable agroecosystems based on the application of ecological principles while considering existing social, cultural, and economic factors of farming communities. (From https://lod.nal.usda.gov/nalt/5505)

The field of physics that explains how extremely small objects simultaneously have the characteristics of both particles (tiny pieces of matter) and waves (a disturbance or variation that transfers energy).
Short summaries of research articles written in clear, easy-to-understand language, intended to be a useful way of communicating health research to a non-expert reader.
The ability to effectively adapt one's cognitive and behavioral strategies in response to changing task or environmental demands. (from Clinical Psychology Review August 2021,102061).

Mixing of several samples together in a batch or pooled sample, then testing the pooled sample with a diagnostic test. This approach increases the number of individuals that can be tested using the same amount of resources.(CDRH-EUA-Templates@fda.hhs.gov)

Health care professionals who render service or treatment, under the direction of or in collaboration with a physician, in accordance with their education and training and State statutes, rules and regulations. Services provided are related to injury and illness prevention, wellness promotion and education, emergent care, examination and clinical diagnosis, therapeutic intervention, and rehabilitation of injuries and medical conditions. (from https://www.bocatc.org/)
Computational designs that apply DEEP LEARNING methods on extremely large data sets as a basis for predicting and constructing natural-sounding text.

Ready-to-eat foods and beverages prepared and/or sold by vendors or hawkers especially in the streets and other similar places. They represent a significant part of urban food consumption for millions of low-and-middle-income consumers, in urban areas on a daily basis. (USDA)

Healthcare pricing information provided in advance of receiving care and publicizing how and from whom patients can obtain price estimates. Hospitals operating in the United States are required to make public a list of standard charges for items and services they provide. (Federal Register 84 FR 65524)
Works about trials in which participants are intentionally challenged (whether or not they have been vaccinated) with exposure to an infectious disease organism.

tarif: Machines that are engineered to learn about their environment and make decisions to complete tasks with little to no human intervention. These robots may be designed to complete tasks such as patient intervention, remote monitoring, inventory transportation, among many others.
Technological systems that perform automated tasks within specific environments enabled by artificial intelligence.

A form of ensemble learning methods which combines weak learners to create strong ones, which reduces training errors and bias in the training models. There are different types of boosting such as gradient boosting, XGBoost, and Adaboost.
A machine learning process used to reduce the number of attributes or features of data (called dimensionality) thereby simplifying understanding of the dataset without a loss in data integrity.

A method in machine learning where several base learners are combined to create an optimal learning model. This can be used for a variety of models including forecasting, classification, or function approximation.

A method of training machine learning models whereby multiple devices train their own copy of the artificial intelligence model using decentralized local data. These locally trained model results are then aggregated by a central server to update the global model without accessing local data.

A machine learning training method in which an agent in an uncertain environment is rewarded for optimal behaviors and punished for undesired behaviors, allowing the agent to learn from trial-and-error.

A class of machine learning approaches that allow a system to discover the representations required for feature detection or classification from raw data. The requirement for manual feature engineering is reduced by allowing a machine to learn the features and apply them to a given activity.
Process of training a new learning network by beginning with previously trained for a related problem, leading to less time and energy required for training the new learning network.
Methods of making prediction about a new measurement based on calculations of previous data.
Machine learning models which are trained to analyze historical data to find patterns and trends, allowing it to predict future outcomes.

A heuristic computational algorithm designed to find optimal solutions in a random search space. Particle swarm optimization measures swarm intelligence which is a computation measurement inspired by behaviors of self-organized swarming animals.

tarif: The process of recognizing and extracting meaningful information from patterns in data. Pattern analysis in machine learning is often used for predictions and forecasting.

Artificial neural networks designed to automatically learn features through the use of sequence of layers which transform one volume to the next. Convolutional neural networks initially produce a feature map by use of convolution layers consisting of a set of learnable filters convolved with input, i.e., having smaller widths and heights and the same depth as that of input volume.

A form of recurrent computer neural networks which allows for important information to be retained and less important information to be erased. These kinds of networks are used for tasks such as language translation, anomaly detection, speech and handwriting recognition, and time series prediction.

A type of neural network that consists of a large number of processing elements called cells arranged in a grid-like structure that interact with each other and neighboring cells through a set of predefined rules to perform complex computations.
A network where information is only passed in one direction. This is the opposite of a recurrent neural network, in which information is processed in a cycle.

A feedforward neural network designed with a single layer hidden node where the weights between inputs and hidden nodes are randomly assigned. Extreme learning machines can be trained fast and used for the data clustering, grouping, regression, prediction, and forecasting.
A feedforward neural network with multiple layers, an input layer, at least three hidden layers, and an output layer, generally used for pattern recognition and classification.
Neural networks designed to process signals supported on graphs.

A three-layer neural network made of an input layer, hidden layer, and output layer. Radial basis function networks are used for function approximation, interpolation, classification, and time series prediction.

A type of neural network where the output from the previous step is fed as input to the current step with the help of a hidden layer which tracks data sequences. Recurrent neural network is often used when the data is sequential, and weights need to be treated same across all the layers such as in time series data and speech recognition. Variation of recurrent neural network include bidirectional neural network and long short-term memory.
Fully interconnected, single layer neural network, which can be used for associative memory and optimization tasks.
Algorithms designed to solve a problem by modifying their behaviors when faced with an unseen task with limited data during training.

An unsupervised learning network which is composed of two separate networks, a generator which produces content and a discriminator which works to identify real content from the generated content. Over time, generative adversarial networks create data that increasingly resembles the input data.
A general algorithmic technique that considers solutions one option at a time backtracking to get the desired solution. This allows searching every possible option recursively.
A class of algorithms that predicts into which category an observation belongs based on training data.
Algorithms designed to find groups of similar data points (called clusters) in the dataset. Clustering is often used for feature engineering or pattern discovery in unsupervised machine learning.
A class of algorithms which both reduces and restores the size of files to increase their portability. Compression algorithms can be lossy or lossless.
Algorithms designed to find or localize the objects in images and assign the objects (affordances).

tarif: Dynamic programming is an optimization technique where smaller portions of problems are broken down, solved, and remembered, in order to solve a larger and more complex problem.

Heuristic search algorithms which direct the random searches to the area of better performance or fitness function by computationally creating the conditions inspired by NATURAL SELECTION. They are commonly used to generate solutions for optimization problems.
A class of algorithms which enables a computer to learn as it goes, thereby accomplishing its goal without being explicitly programmed to do so.
Algorithms that can execute several instructions simultaneously on different processing devices and then combine all the individual outputs to produce the final result.
A class of algorithms which are designed to forecast unseen data. Prediction Algorithms can discover patterns, perform classification tasks, and identify trends.

An unsupervised learning technique where the machine learns patterns in unlabeled data sets, makes compressed representations and reconstructs the input as output at minimum loss of features from the input. Autoencoders are useful in denoising images, DIMENSIONALITY REDUCTION and feature extraction.

Finite learnable stochastic models often used in MACHINE LEARNING consisting of two processes: a MARKOV CHAIN and an event observed and analyzed in a state unknown or hidden to the observer. Hidden Markov Models are often used in BIOINFORMATICS, time series analysis and speech and handwriting recognition.
Weakly supervised learning algorithms where training set is arranged in a labeled bag of instances, and a single class label is assigned to a bag.

Persistent and irrational fear of enclosed places (e.g., elevators, closets, tunnels) or of being confined (e.g., in an airplane or the backseat of a car). Situations where enclosure or confinement may be encountered are often avoided or else endured with intense anxiety or distress. The focus of fear is typically on panic symptoms triggered in these situations, such as feelings of being unable to breathe, choking, sweating, and fears of losing control. (From APA Dictionary of Psychology, accessed 11/8/2023)

Overwhelming and persistent reluctance to go to school, which usually occurs during the primary school years and is often a symptom of an educational, social, or emotional problem. (From APA Dictionary of Psychology)

Situations in which two moral principles conflict with one another. Fictional or hypothetical dilemmas of this kind are used to assess the moral beliefs or moral reasoning skills of individuals. (From APA Dictionary of Psychology, https://dictionary.apa.org/)

A type of TELEMEDICINE in which healthcare providers monitor patients using digital medical devices. Data collected from these devices are then electronically transferred to providers for care management and has been used to measure symptoms of chronic conditions, such as cardiac diseases, diabetes, and asthma. Benefits include patient engagement, patient adherence to their treatment plan, and the ability to expand physician reach and easily provide care to patients without the need for patients in person encounters. (From https://psnet.ahrq.gov/perspective/remote-patient-monitoring. Accessed 11 Nov 2023)
The subjective perception and evaluation of one’s own body in terms of different aspects such as size, shape, musculature or muscle tone, weight, and fitness.

Professionals trained in the study of mental processes and behavior in man and animals.

Authorization allowing the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to strengthen public health protections against chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats including infectious diseases, by facilitating the availability and use of medical countermeasures needed during public health emergencies. Under section 564 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, FDA may authorize unapproved medical products or unapproved uses of approved medical products to be used in an emergency to diagnose, treat, or prevent serious or life-threatening diseases or  agents when certain criteria are met, including there are no adequate, approved, and available alternatives.(From fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/emergency-use-authorization-medical-products-and-related-authorities)
Removal of the TRACHEOSTOMY tube.

Meningitis caused by a fungus of the genus COCCIDIOIDES, endemic to the SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES, south-central Washington State, and parts of Mexico and Central and South America.

INTERLEUKINS that affect the differentiation and function of LYMPHOCYTES and MYELOID CELLS and regulate both IMMUNITY, INNATE and ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY. They are also involved in the expansion of NK CELLS.

Enzymes that catalyze the transfer of GMP residue from GTP to 5' end of RNA to form a cap structure identified as G(5')pppN. They can also modify synthetic poly(A) & poly(G) to form m7G(5')pppAn & m7G(5')pppGn.
A systematic training calendar designed to provide variations in performance targeting, while maximizing results and reducing the potential for overtraining. Term only applies to EXERCISE.

Information or entertainment in digital form, especially online via the Internet. Examples of digital media include online news sources, video games, blogs, and social media. The term may also be used to describe online content, especially content that is interactive; on-demand media that is accessible through a range of devices; and media that is responded to or shared in real time. It is sometimes used to refer to content that is created, published, or distributed by individuals or non-traditional publishers, such as bloggers.

A laboratory technique for determining the DNA sequence of an organism's genome. In this approach, DNA of an organism is randomly broken into small DNA fragments which are then sequenced individually. Computational methods are then utilized to reassemble these sequenced fragments accurately, reconstructing the complete genome sequence.

A rare, malignant MELANOMA arising from the melanocytes of the UVEA.
A minimally invasive water ablation procedure used for treating BENIGN PROSTATE HYPERPLASIA. During this procedure, a robotically controlled water jet is used to remove excess prostate tissue.
A form of EUROPEAN FOOTBALL derived from traditional Irish ball games. It has similarities to, but is distinct from, SOCCER and RUGBY.
Forced labor occurs when individuals are compelled against their will to provide work or service through the use of force, fraud, or coercion.  (https://www.dhs.gov/blue-campaign/forced-labor)
Treatment that helps a person work through a greater than normal reaction to a loss, such as the death of a loved one.  Therapy may be individual or group therapy.

diger_kavramlar.tarif: Grief counseling the provision of advice, information, and psychological support to help individuals whose ability to function has been impaired by someone’s death, particularly that of a loved one or friend. It includes counseling for the grieving process and practical advice concerning arrangements for the funeral and burial of the loved one. Grief counseling is sometimes offered by staff in specialized agencies (e.g., hospices), or it may be carried out in the context of other counseling. (https://dictionary.apa.org/grief-counseling)

tarif: Methods used by specialized onco-anesthesiologists in the perioperative care of patients undergoing cancer-related diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. The aim is to minimize preoperative complications, expedite recovery, and facilitate early return to intended oncological treatment.

Disease that affects linguistic, VISUAL SPATIAL PROCESSING; EXECUTIVE FUNCTION, and MOOD regulation. Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome is associated with acquired lesions in the CEREBELLUM particularly in the posterior lobe and the vermis.

Infection of the lungs in a patient who is not hospitalized or who has not resided in a long-term care facility for 14 days prior to the onset of symptoms. It is associated with some signs and symptoms of acute infection and is accompanied by the presence of an acute infiltrate on chest radiograph.(US Pharm. 2007;32(10):44-5 https://www.uspharmacist.com/article/community-acquired-pneumonia)

The collection, transformation, and organization of data in order to draw conclusions, make predictions, and drive informed decision making. The process deduces logical sets and patterns by filtering and applying required transformations and models of raw data.

The use of engineered small molecules to manipulate the activity of specific cells within living organisms, typically. Chemogenetic techniques are often used to study specific neural activity through genetically engineered receptors that bind specific endogenous or exogenous ligands.

Molecular probes that respond to specific chemical interactions by altering the degree or frequency of their fluorescence. They are used to provide direct visualization of chemical changes within cells.

Acute often necrotizing pyelonephritis characterized by accumulation of gas within and around renal parenchyma. Emphysematous pyelonephritis is typically associated with bacterial infection in DIABETES MELLITUS and IMMUNOCOMPROMISED PATIENT.
A genetic engineering technique that involves manipulating the EPIGENOME at the target region with minimal or no modification of the genomic DNA.
Rare abnormality where a fetal part of an identical twin that stopped developing during gestation is found within a normally developing fetus. It is considered a TWIN PREGNANCY complication.

The Higher Education Act of 1965, as amended, defines an HBCU as: “…any historically black college or university that was established prior to 1964, whose principal mission was, and is, the education of black Americans, and that is accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting agency or association determined by the Secretary [of Education] to be a reliable authority as to the quality of training offered or is, according to such an agency or association, making reasonable progress toward accreditation.” (https://sites.ed.gov/whhbcu/one-hundred-and-five-historically-black-colleges-and-universities/
The use of drugs to enhance or sustain sexual activity primarily but not exclusively by men who have sex with men.

diger_kavramlar.tarif: Sexualized intravenous drug use.

tarif: A rare congenital malformation that affects the development of the urinary, digestive, and REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEMS due to CLOACA malformations. In this condition, the large intestine develops outside the abdominal cavity, with the bladder connected to it. Due to this abnormal connection between the colon and the bladder, urine and stool can mix, and there is often no anus.
Technicians who follow prescriptions for visual correction, order lenses, and dispense eyeglasses and contact lenses.
Injuries to RNA molecules, leading to changes in their structure or function.

Perception or feeling of control over one's own actions thereby influencing the course of events and outcomes. SELF-EFFICACY on the other hand is beliefs or expectations in self-ability to achieve intended goals or to produce a given effect in specific tasks.
A therapeutic intervention designed to improve PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING through reduced ANXIETY; PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS; DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS; DISTRESS and improved mood by increased mindfulness.
A therapeutic intervention designed to treat people with DEPRESSION through use of elements of MINDFULNESS-BASED STRESS REDUCTION and other cognitive behavioral therapy.
Persistent and difficult to control psychological distress over CLIMATE CHANGE.
Death of a pregnant or birthing person during pregnancy or up to one year after the end of pregnancy from health issues related to pregnancy.
The practice of medicine concerned with conditions in individuals resulting from exposure to environments where the ambient pressure is increased, such as the undersea environment.

Corticotropin Releasing Hormone Receptor 1 is a G protein coupled receptor that binds corticotropin-releasing hormone, a peptide that plays a key role in activating signal transduction pathways involved in the stress response.

A multifunctional protein primarily found in the PLASMA with His/Pro-Rich (HRR) region which contains approximately 12 tandem internal repeats of the 5-residue G[H/P][H/P]PH consensus sequence. Histidine-rich glycoprotein has a diverse range of ligands that are involved in many biological processes, including COAGULATION; IMMUNE RESPONSE; ANGIOGENESIS, and WOUND HEALING.
Glycosyltransferases involved in the elongation of HEPARAN SULFATE chains. Mutations in exostosin genes are associated with HEREDITARY MULTIPLE EXOSTOSES.
Outcome anticipated or expected due to various qualities of a healthcare treatment.
Believed or anticipated consequences of a person’s behavior.

A healthcare framework that typically integrates clinical information systems to improve CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING, support for COMMUNITY RESOURCES and SELF-MANAGEMENT and improvement of care continuity through better delivery system design and organization.

A bifunctional glycosyltransferase involved in transferring GLUCURONIC ACID and N-ACETYLGLUCOSAMINE in the elongation of HEPARAN SULFATE chains. Mutations in the gene EXT1, coding for this protein (as well as mutations in other genes), are responsible for defects in heparan sulfate synthesis resulting in HEREDITARY MULTIPLE EXOSTOSES. Exostosin-1, along with EXOSTOSIN-2, is a component of heparan sulfate polymerase.
Various interventions designed to improve treatment adherence and compliance.

A combination of defects comprising OMPHALOCELE, exstrophy of the cloaca, ANUS IMPERFORATE, and spinal defects. This rare complex is thought to represent the most severe end of a spectrum of birth defects, the exstrophy-epispadias sequence, which, in order of increasing severity, includes phallic separation with EPISPADIAS, pubic diastasis, EXSTROPHY OF THE BLADDER, and CLOACAL EXSTROPHY. (From OMIM 258040)
giris_terimleri: Omphalocele Exstrophy Imperforate Anus Spinal Defects Complex
Omphalocele, Exstrophy Of The Bladder, Imperforate Anus, Spinal Abnormalities
Omphalocele, Exstrophy Of The Cloaca, Imperforate Anus, and Spinal Defects

tarif: A bifunctional glycosyltransferase involved in transferring GLUCURONIC ACID and N-ACETYLGLUCOSAMINE in the elongation of HEPARAN SULFATE chains. Mutations in the gene EXT2, coding for this protein (as well as mutations in other genes), are responsible for defects in heparan sulfate synthesis resulting in chromosome 11-linked HEREDITARY MULTIPLE EXOSTOSES. Exostosin 2, along with EXOSTOSIN 1, is a component of heparan sulfate polymerase.

Loss of the MAXILLA bone mass and/or height due to natural edentulous maxilla (JAW, EDENTULOUS) or previous dental extractions. It may require a reconstruction via BONE TRANSPLANTATION and/or ALVEOLOPLASTY prior to a DENTAL IMPLANTATION.

A rare and aggressive hematologic malignancy derived from the precursors of PLASMACYTOID DENDRITIC CELLS. Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasms affect bone marrow and blood in addition to the lymph nodes, spleen, central nervous system, and skin.
giris_terimleri: Agranular CD4+ CD56+ Hematodermic Neoplasm Tumor
Agranular CD4+ Natural Killer Cell Leukemia

tarif: A photochemical injury to retina tissues, usually at the RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM. It is commonly associated with sungazing, eclipse viewing, welding, or using a laser pointer without proper eye protection resulting in subjective visual disturbances (e.g., floaters) and reduced VISUAL ACUITY.

Allergic reaction to certain foods, including fresh fruits, vegetables and nuts which share CROSS REACTIONS to allergens from trees, grass or pollens. Oral allergy syndrome is limited to itchy lips, mouth, and throat without severe ANAPHYLAXIS and is often associated with chronic EOSINOPHILIC ESOPHAGITIS.

The return of individual results involves the return of information specific to the research subject. It encompasses information that is linked to the identity of a research subject and pertains to that subject and the focus of the study. Individual results can be obtained in clinical, social behavioral, and other types of research is not limited to clinical research (https://www.hhs.gov/ohrp/sachrp-committee/recommendations/attachment-b-return-individual-research-results/index.html).
giris_terimleri: Return of Research Results to Study Participants

tarif: Co-occurrence of DIABETES MELLITUS and OBESITY largely due to diabetic complication from HYPERGLYCEMIA. Diabesity is also associated with faster deterioration of diabetic symptoms and complications.
Generally an issue or an institution emerging into the sphere of politics such as making previously unpolitical matters political. (Tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/13501763.2019.1619188)

A way of referring people to non-clinical local services (for example, sports activities, arts, group learning, community-based activities, cookery and gardening), with the sole aim of ensuring human contact, followed by support and care.

Surface-active substances produced by plants and microorganisms, such as bacteria, fungi, and yeast. They have the ability to reduce surface and INTERFACIAL TENSION, making them useful in a variety of applications.
A process where chemical reactions are carried out in a continuously flowing stream rather than in batch production.

The clinical application of SYSTEMS BIOLOGY, that focuses on identifying the underlying drivers of a patient's disease and addressing, through personalized therapeutic interventions, those root causes of the disease.
Sitting or walking in a FOREST or forested area and taking in all of the environmental stimuli of the forest - the sounds, images, atmospheric conditions, etc. as a form of therapy.
A left-handed conformation of double stranded RNA that is similar in structure to Z-DNA.

A portable imaging device used to perform radiographic examinations outside the traditional radiology department. Mobile X-ray machines provide diagnostic imaging when patients cannot be easily moved or in locations that lack permanent imaging facilities.
Lipid mediators derived from derivatives of POLYUNSATURATED FATTY ACIDS which tends to limit inflammation. They include resolvins, PROTECTIN, maresins, and LIPOXINS.
Digital certificates, in the form of data recorded on a BLOCKCHAIN, that signify ownership of associated digital items, such as images, music, or videos, not contained in the certificate data itself.
Pregnancy in women at least 35 years old at the time of delivery. This was formerly known as geriatric pregnancy.

diger_kavramlar.ad: Pregnancy at Age 35 Years or Older
terimler: Pregnancy at Age 35 Years or Older

tarif: A rare form of dilated cardiomyopathy which causes heart enlargement and weakness during the last month of pregnancy or within five months of delivery.
Surgeries on the the COLON; RECTUM; and ANAL CANAL.
The facilitation of verbal communication to assist in the healthcare process, by converting a message in one language to the same message in another language.
Places where alcoholic beverages are served.
To continue to live in one's home safely, independently, and comfortably in a familiar environment..

Works consisting of meta-analysis of randomized trials in which estimates of comparative treatment effects are visualized and interpreted from a network of interventions that may or may not have been evaluated directly against each other. Common considerations in network meta-analysis include conceptual and statistical heterogeneity and incoherence.
Products used to maintain hygiene, health, and appearance.
A synthetic porous ultralight solid material is created from a gel through a supercritical drying process, in which the gel's liquid component is replaced with gas.

diger_kavramlar.tarif: The SILICA combined with a solvent to create a gel.

tarif: A technique for delivering therapeutic compounds into the body through the skin with minimal invasiveness.
Vertigo or major dizziness associated with abnormal brain activity in migraine affecting the VESTIBULAR SYSTEM.
A physical characteristic of an organism's sex that is not directly related to its REPRODUCTIVE SYSTEM.

A physiological response to awakening. It is a discreet and distinct component of the CORTISOL circadian cycle, with characteristics unrelated to cortisol secretion throughout the rest of the day (Wilhelm et al., 2007; Fries et al., 2009).

A chronic functional disorder with vertigo, dizziness and unsteadiness triggered by vestibular episode and psychological stress. Unlike in BENIGN PAROXYSMAL POSITIONAL VERTIGO, the otoliths on the OTOLITHIC MEMBRANE are not involved in pathology of persistent postural-perceptual dizziness.

An abnormal connection between inner ear and the surrounding structures, resulting in a leakage of the PERILYMPH. It is most common in a whiplash-type head trauma injury. Perilymph or labyrinthine fistulas may result in dizziness and/or intermittent hearing loss.

Inner ear diseases caused by autoimmune reaction, characterized by audiovestibular dysfunction including TINNITUS; VERTIGO and progressive SENSORINEURAL HEARING LOSS. Autoimmune inner ear disease may coexist with other systemic autoimmune diseases (e.g., COGAN SYNDROME).

Presence of vestibular symptoms such as light-headedness, dizziness or unsteadiness associated with injuries and pathologies of the CERVICAL VERTEBRAE. Cervicogenic dizziness are often associated with a whiplash-type injury and neck pain.
The reduction of the immunogenicity of a population of tumor cells over time, under the GENETIC SELECTION pressure of IMMUNOLOGIC SURVEILLANCE, leading to TUMOR IMMUNE EVASION.
Tests in which two tasks are performed simultaneously. Dual-Task Exercises can be used to show the performance differences of subjects in MULTITASKING BEHAVIOR.
Materials produced from CARBON with a unit size typically between 1 and 100 nanometers.
Spherical carbon materials typically less than 10 nanometers in size and possessing fluorescence emission properties.
A reproductive process where a SURROGATE MOTHER carries and gives birth to a child for another person or couple.

diger_kavramlar.tarif: A type of surrogacy where the surrogate has no genetic connection to the child. An embryo created through FERTILIZATION IN VITRO, using the egg and sperm of the intended parents (or donors), is implanted in her UTERUS.
A type of surrogacy where the surrogate is biologically related to the child because her own egg is used. The surrogate is artificially inseminated with sperm from the intended father or a donor.

tarif: A strategy used in PHARMACEUTIC CHEMISTRY where one part of a molecule is replaced with a different one that has similar physical or chemical properties, but with the aim of enhancing the biological activity, stability, or safety of the molecule.

A signaling pathway that enables cells to adapt to various stressors by modulating protein synthesis. It is initiated by the activation of specific PROTEIN KINASES (e.g., PERK, GCN2, PKR, and HRI) in response to distinct stress signals, including amino acid deprivation, VIRAL INFECTIONS, and OXIDATIVE STRESS.
The ability to hear and distinguish one SOUND from another. These are typically assessed using whisper tests, tuning fork tests, or BONE CONDUCTION tests.
The altered pattern of GENE EXPRESSION related to RNA METHYLATION.
Enlargement of the lips most often by injection of DERMAL FILLER.
The study of the structure, function, and biology of carbohydrates (sugars) and carbohydrate-containing molecules, known as glycans, in biological systems.
A healthcare professional specializing in evaluating and treating patients with airway and breathing problems.
The systematic study of the global GENE EXPRESSION changes due to changes in the EPITRANSCRIPTOME and not due to RNA base sequence changes.
A specialized transport barrier between the PARENCHYMAL TISSUE of the SPINAL CORD and the surrounding BLOOD VESSELS.
Graphic visual representations of educational content. It is used to deliver complex information, such as RESEARCH results.

Meshwork of extracellular matrix containing CHONDROITIN SULFATE PROTEOGLYCANS structures interposed among glial processes. Perineuronal nets (PNN) surround the soma and dendrites of certain neuronal cell types, e.g., inhibitory GABAergic PARVALBUMIN-positive INTERNEURONS. PNN plays a role in NEURONAL PLASTICITY and may modulate memory.
Blood vessels in the host site targeted to receive blood from transplanted tissue or SURGICAL FLAPS in various procedures, e.g., MICROSURGERY; PLASTIC SURGERY PROCEDURES; and SURGICAL ANASTOMOSIS.

The presence of one or more thin flap-like membranes arising from the posterior wall of the INTERNAL CAROTID ARTERY bulb. While carotid webs can be asymptomatic, they may also be associated with TRANSIENT ISCHEMIC ATTACKS, and STROKE.
A diagnostic test primarily used to detect TUBERCULOSIS and other respiratory infections.

A process where the genome of a pathogen is studied to find genes that may code for antigen proteins. If found, the putative antigen genes are then cloned, expressed in bacteria, and used to vaccinate experimental animals. If the expressed protein is shown to induce protective immunity it then becomes a candidate for further studies as a vaccine to be used to prevent infection.
Nanostructures formed from DNA. They are used as a scaffold for complex structures due to programmable assembly and control of size, shape, and function.

diger_kavramlar.tarif: NANOSTRUCTURES synthesized by using DNA scaffolds with short synthetic DNA staples to control their shapes.

tarif: MILK SUBSTITUITES derived from PLANTS.
Maintaining comfortable temperature for living in general, and more specifically for patients in hospitals.
A tailorable technique of infusing YTTRIUM 90 (Y90) for hepatocellular carcinoma treatment with continuous restaging.
Longitudinal Studies done in Canada on Ageing Populations
An immune disease that is triggered by a variety of ADJUVANTS. It results in a spectrum of autoimmune and inflammatory responses that lead to significant health challenges.
giris_terimleri: Autoimmune Inflammatory Syndrome Induced by Adjuvants

tarif: The state of the VASCULAR SYSTEM when functioning optimally without evidence of disease, disorders, or deficiencies.

Glucuronosyltransferase encoded by UGT1 complex which encodes human bilirubin, phenol, and other UDP-glucuronosyltransferase isozymes with identical carboxyl termini. It catalyzes reactions where lipophilic substrates are conjugated with glucuronic acid to increase the metabolite's water solubility and excretion into either urine or bile. UGT1A1enzyme is essential for elimination and detoxification of drugs, xenobiotics and metabolites.

A cytoskeletal protein and PROTEIN-TYROSINE KINASE substrate that links cytoskeletal structures to the PLASMA MEMBRANE. In EPITHELIAL CELLS, it is essential for the formation of MICROVILLI and membrane ruffles on the apical pole and is also required for macropinocytosis (see PINOCYTOSIS) along with the GUANINE NUCLEOTIDE EXCHANGE FACTOR PLEKHG6.
An ORPHAN NUCLEAR RECEPTOR that is activated by farnesol metabolites in bile acid; Increases insulin production and sensitivity.
MAP kinase kinase kinase which plays a critical role in cellular responses to environmental stimuli and CYTOKINES.
A classical cadherin which plays a critical role in maintaining permeability of the ENDOTHELIUM.

A family of ACUTE PHASE PROTEINS characterized by a shared pentraxin PROTEIN DOMAIN. They include C-reactive protein and serum amyloid P component and function in the regulation of INNATE IMMUNITY and INFLAMMATION.

Viruses with a monopartitite or bipartite positive-strand RNA genome that share the following properties: auto-proteolytically processed polyprotein(s), a common three-domain replication block (Hel-Pro-Pol domain consisting of a superfamily III helicase, a proteinase with a chymotrypsin-like structure and a superfamily I RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) and non-enveloped icosahedral virions approximately 30 nm in diameter with a pseudo-T=3 symmetry.
A superoxide dismutase that processes REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES generated by mitochondrial respiration. It protects tissues from damage during disease progression.
The catalyst to phosphorylate SPHINGOSINE into sphingosine-1-phosphate; Important in ANGIOGENESIS, CELL SURVIVAL, and CELL MIGRATION
A proteoglycan involved in joint surface lubrication and encoded by the PRG4 gene. Altered expression occurs in some forms of ARTHRITIS.
A tacrolimus binding protein with peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase activity that interacts with PROGESTERONE RECEPTOR complexes and HSP90 HEAT-SHOCK PROTEINS.
A bacterial repressor protein that has serine endopeptidase activity. LexA represses transcription of genes involved in the SOS RESPONSE to DNA DAMAGE.

An inwardly-rectifying potassium channel that forms the pore of KATP CHANNELS. It regulates potassium permeability as a function of cytoplasmic ATP and ADP concentrations in many different cell types.

A basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor that regulates expression of genes in response to oxygen, including VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR. It plays a role in the development of blood vessels (NEOVASCULARIZATION, PHYSIOLOGIC) and lung tissue.

A myosin-binding protein found in the SARCOMERES of STRIATED MUSCLE. Iit has slow and fast paralogs. Myosin-binding protein C regulates systolic and diastolic activity in MYOCARDIUM and muscle contraction in SKELETAL MUSCLE.
A non-invasive and radiation-free imaging modality that detects superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) to create high-contrast, real-time images.
A phenomenon where a muscle's force output is temporarily enhanced due to its previous contraction history.
Synthetic, water-soluble acrylic polymers with the formula -CH2CHCONH2-.
A large, gelatin-degrading membrane SERINE ENDOPEPTIDASE complex expressed by stromal FIBROBLASTS of epithelial cancers; it is a biomarker for MELANOMA cell invasiveness.
A component of TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR AP-1; do not confuse with fibrinogen-related antigen (FRA antigen)
A dinucleoside triphosphate hydrolase that has a critical role in regulating the expression of genes essential for CELL PROLIFERATION; CELL SURVIVAL, and modulating APOPTOSIS.

A cation transport protein that shares structural homology with prokaryotic and eukaryotic transport proteins. In mammals, it is a MACROPHAGE-specific antiporter, transporting metal ions in either direction against a proton gradient, and localizes to membranes of late ENDOSOMES and LYSOSOMES, where it may contribute to antimicrobial activity.
giris_terimleri: Solute Carrier Family 11-(proton-coupled divalent metal ion transporters), Member 1

tarif: A neurotrophic protein and serpin that induces CELL DIFFERENTIATION in RETINOBLASTOMA cells and also functions as an ANGIOGENESIS INHIBITOR in the mammalian eye.
giris_terimleri: Early Population Doubling Level Cdna-1 ProteinEarly Population Doubling Level Cdna-1 Protein

tarif: A mammalian endoglucuronidase which degrades HEPARAN SULFATE glycosaminoglycans into short 5-6 kDa pieces.

A protein that binds to certain BONE MORPHOGENIC PROTEINS to regulate their activity. In Xenopus embryos, this is a dorsalizing factor localized to the SPEMANN ORGANIZER. Mutations in this protein may occur in NOG-RELATED-SYMPHALANGISM SPECTRUM DISORDER.
A ubiquitin regulator which encodes a coiled-coil domain that interacts with STATHMIN and is involved in endosomal protein sorting

A cis-trans isomerase that catalyzes the isomerization of all trans-retinol to 11-cis-retinol (VITAMIN A) in the dark. It is expressed in the RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM and also converts ALL-TRANS-RETINYL ESTERS to 11-cis-retinol.

A secreted glycoprotein that controls activation of signaling pathways in adjacent cells (PARACRINE COMMUNICATION) for processes that include CELL ADHESION; CELL MIGRATION; and organization of the CYTOSKELETON. It is primarily expressed in the RETINA and variants in the myocillin gene cause GLAUCOMA 1, OPEN ANGLE, A.
An interleukin that suppresses MELANOMA cell growth and colony formation. ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM STRESS activates its expression.

A C-type lectin that functions as a pattern recognition receptor on DENDRITIC CELLS and other immune cells. It is specific for beta-1,-linked and beta 1,6-linked GLUCANS that constitute the CELL WALL of pathogenic bacteria and fungi, and is essential for the TOLL-LIKE RECEPTOR 2 INNATE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE and activation of NF-KAPPA-B.
Phosphoric monoester hydrolases that dephosphorylate PHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOLS to regulate CELL SIGNALING.
A component of TRANSPORT VESICLES that contain GLUT4 PROTEIN. It functions in the transport and processing of LDL RECEPTORS.

Serine-threonine-protein kinases that regulates a variety of ION CHANNELS and MEMBRANE TRANSPORT PROTEINS, as well as cellular processes that include neuronal excitability, CELL PROLIFERATION; CELL SURVIVAL;  and APOPTOSIS. They also have important roles in the cellular stress response (STRESS, PHYSIOLOGICAL), renal sodium retention and potassium elimination.
An interferon regulatory factor regulated by INTERFERON-GAMMA that binds the interferon-inducible ENHANCER ELEMENTS of HISTOCOMPATIBILITY ANTIGENS CLASS I genes.

A histone deacetylase that catalyzes the deacetylation of the core HISTONES (H2A, H2B,H3, and H4) as well as other cellular proteins. It functions in the CELL NUCLEUS as part of the nuclear-receptor corepressor complex to regulate the GENETIC TRANSCRIPTION of NUCLEAR RECEPTORS.
The major structural protein of vault ribonucleoprotein particles, which function in NUCLEOCYTOPLASMIC TRANSPORT and SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION.

The terminal OXIDOREDUCTASE in the plant mitochondrial electron transport chain utilized in the alternative pathway of respiration. It limits REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES production and bypasses ELECTRON TRANSPORT COMPLEX III and ELECTRON TRANSPORT COMPLEX IV to keep metabolic homeostasis during PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS.

A lysophospholipase that catalyzes the hydrolysis of GLYCEROPHOSPHOLIPIDS to produce LYSOPHOSPHATIDIC ACIDS and corresponding AMINES. Autotaxin is secreted lysophospholipase D and produces lysophosphatidic acid in EXTRACELLULAR FLUID.

A serine-threonine protein kinase that functions in many different processes including the cellular response to PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS, production of CYTOKINES; ENDOCYTOSIS; CYTOSKELETON dynamics, CELL MIGRATION; and CELL PROLIFERATION. It is phosphorylated by MAPK14 in response to stress, and in turn phosphorylates substrates at a SERINE that is preceded by a large hydrophobic amino acid.
An activation antigen and C-type lectin that is rapidly induced and phosphorylated after IL-2 stimulation of NK CELLS and a subset of low buoyant density T-LYMPHOCYTES.

Rab GTP-binding proteins that function primarily in regulating intracellular PROTEIN TRANSPORT among membrane-bound ORGANELLES and in ENDOCYTOSIS. They also participate in the establishment of CELL POLARITY in EPITHELIAL CELLS.
A glucagon-like peptide and GLP-1 agonist used to enhance glycemic control of TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS, and for OBESITY MANAGEMENT.

A signal transduction pathway that involves cGMP-AMP synthase (cGAS), stimulator of interferon genes (STING), and downstream signaling adaptors. This pathway plays an essential role in the innate immune system by activating immune defenses, particularly against invading pathogens or harmful damage.

A membrane protein that functions in INNATE IMMUNITY and INFLAMMATION through the CGAS-STING SIGNALING PATHWAY. It acts as a sensor of cytosolic DNA from bacteria and viruses and promotes the production of INTERFERON TYPE I.

A scaffold protein originally thought to function as a SERINE-THREONINE PROTEIN KINASE. It lacks kinase activity and regulates a variety of cellular processes that include CELL ADHESION; CELL MIGRATION; and assembly of FOCAL ADHESIONS.
A thymosin that functions to regulate organization of the CYTOSKELETON. It binds to and sequesters ACTIN monomers to inhibit POLYMERIZATION and also inhibits CELL DIFFERENTIATION of some STEM CELLS.

A serine-threonine-protein kinase which senses damaged MITOCHONDRIA and protects against mitochondrial dysfunction caused by PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS. It phosphorylates proteins on the OUTER MITOCHONDRIAL MEMBRANE to coordinate quality control mechanisms that remove and replace dysfunctional mitochondrial components. Mutations in the PINK1 gene, which encodes PTEN-induced putative kinase, are associated with PARKINSON DISEASE.
A developmental process in which NEURONS extend and form SYNAPSES.
A therapeutic approach that focuses on modulating the host's immunity or interfering with cell mechanisms necessary for pathogen function, rather than focusing on pathogens themselves.
A cytoplasmic autoantigen and ribonucleoprotein implicated in nascent RNA protection. It is a target of AUTOANTIBODIES in patients with SJOGREN'S SYNDROME.
A ubiquitin-protein ligase that supports INNATE IMMUNITY by binding to the invariant chain of antibody-virus complexes. It prevents expression of viral genes.
Proteins that cotransport sodium ions and iodide ions across cellular membranes. They function in the biosynthesis of TRIIODOTHYRONINE and THYROXINE.
A G-PROTEIN-COUPLED RECEPTOR found in RETINAL GANGLION CELLS that regulates non-image forming visual functions like CIRCADIAN RHYTHM responses and pupil dilation.

A regulatory membrane peptide of SARCOPLASMIC RETICULUM CALCIUM-TRANSPORTING ATPASES. Its phosphorylation by CYCLIC AMP-DEPENDENT PROTEIN KINASES allows protein kinase-induced stimulation of calcium transport.

A subclass of retinol-binding proteins that take part in the transport of RETINOL between the ROD CELL OUTER SEGMENT and RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM. Do not confuse with inverted repeat binding protein (also known as IRBP).

A pathogen pattern recognition receptor and C-type lectin expressed on the surface of immature DENDRITIC CELLS (DCs). It also functions as a high-affinity receptor for intercellular adhesion molecules ICAM-2 and ICAM-3 to initiate the primary IMMUNE RESPONSE.
Transmembrane proteoglycans expressed in OLIGODENDROCYTE PRECURSOR CELLS; NEUROGLIA: and PERICYTES. It is a biomarker and treatment target for MELANOMA.
A type of regulated cell death that is triggered by the accumulation of COPPER in MITOCHONDRIA.
An interferon regulatory factor that is key in immune CELL DIFFERENTIATION, LYMPHOCYTE ACTIVATION, and generating ANTIBODY-PRODUCING CELLS. They play a key role in the development of DENDRITIC CELLS.

A secretion produced by honey BEES that consists of water, protein, MONOSACCHARIDES; and FATTY ACIDS that include 10-hydroxy-2-decenoic acid, sebacic acid, 10-hydroxydecanoic acid, and  9-oxo-2-decanoic acid. It also contains trace amounts of MINERALS; ANTI-BACTERIAL COMPOUNDS; B VITAMINS; and VITAMIN C.
A minimally invasive procedure for delivering aerosolized chemotherapy into the PERITONEUM.
A serine-threonine protein kinase that induces phosphorylation & inactivation of NF-KAPPAB INHIBITOR ALPHA in vitro.

An extracellular matrix protein that binds FIBRILLAR COLLAGENS and functions in CELL ADHESION; CELL MIGRATION; and CELL PROLIFERATION. In humans, the TGFBI gene encodes beta IG-H3 protein, and mutations in TGFBI cause CORNEAL DYSTROPHIES, HEREDITARY.

A p300-CBP transcription factor with intrinsic HISTONE ACETYLASE activity that functions to promote TRANSCRIPTIONAL ACTIVATION. Among its functions is suppression of the CELL CYCLE where it competes with ADENOVIRUS E1A PROTEINS.
An HIV integrase inhibitor that is used in the treatment of HIV INFECTIONS in combination with other ANTI-HIV AGENTS.
A carbocyclic nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor with potent and selective anti-HIV activity.

An acetyltransferase that transfers an acetyl group to SPERMIDINE as it is converted into PUTRESCINE. It occurs in two types: the cytosolic N1-acetyltransferse (cSAT) and the nuclear N8-acetyltransferase (nSAT).
A repressor protein that restricts neuronal gene transcription in non-neuronal cells.

An acute-phase protein that binds to the lipid a moiety of bacterial LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDES, a glycolipid present in the outer membrane of all GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA. The Lipopolysaccharide-Binding Proteins/Lipopolysaccharide complex may be involved in immune response by interacting with the CD14 ANTIGEN

An ETS MOTIF - containing trans-activator that functions in HEMATOPOIESIS. It activates transcription of critical genes by making genomic regions within HETEROCHROMATIN accessible to other key transcription factors.

A bi-directional monocarboxylic acid transporter that occurs in many different tissues, including MYOCARDIUM; LYMPHOCYTES; and MONOCYTES. It catalyzes transport across the PLASMA MEMBRANE of monocarboxylates such as LACTATE; PYRUVATE; ACETATE; and KETONE BODIES.
giris_terimleri: Solute Carrier Family 16 (Monocarboxylic Acid Transporters), Member 1 Protein

tarif: A nucleotidyltransferase that catalyzes the formation of cyclic GMP-AMP in mammals. This activates the STING1 PROTEIN through the CGAS-STING SIGNALING PATHWAY, which triggers the production of INTERFERON TYPE I and other CYTOKINES.
A cation transport protein that is important in metal transport, particularly iron, in MACROPHAGES. It is important in intestinal iron absorption and supplying iron for ERYTHROCYTES.
giris_terimleri: Solute Carrier Family 11- (Proton-Coupled Divalent Metal Ion Transporters), Member 2

tarif: Monosaccharide transport proteins that move cytosolic URIDINE DIPHOSPHATE GALACTOSE into the Golgi apparatus by exchanging it for URIDINE MONOPHOSPHATE. They can also transport URIDINE DIPHOSPHATE N-ACETYLGALACTOSAMINE.
Facilities other than traditional PHARMACIES that provide medicinal products to people in a hospital setting, or at a retail location.
A cysteine endopeptidase that occurs in LYSOSOMES of MACROPHAGES where it hydrolyzes molecules containing ASPARAGINE. It plays a critical role in ANTIGEN PRESENTATION.
An atrial natriuretic factor receptor that regulates cardiac growth. It has a binding preference for NATRIURETIC PEPTIDE, C-TYPE.

A condition that is characterized by episodes of sudden uncontrollable and inappropriate laughing or crying. It can result from certain neurological conditions or injuries that may impact the way the brain controls emotions.

A congenital defect with major fissure in the ABDOMINAL WALL at the UMBILICUS resulting in the extrusion of VISCERA through the UMBILICUS. Unlike GASTROSCHISIS, omphalocele is covered with PERITONEUM but without overlying SKIN.

A group of barrel-shaped imidazolines composed of (n) glycoluril monomers linked by methylene bridges and are often abbreviated CB[n] or CB*[n]. They have a high binding affinity to CATIONS and neutral molecules.
An amino acid transport protein that acts as a SYMPORTER transporting taurine with sodium across the CELL MEMBRANE. It plays a role in the metabolism of NEUROTRANSMITTER AGENTS.

A member of the S100 family of calcium-binding proteins that binds BCL-XL PROTEIN. It acts as a PLASMINOGEN receptor that mediates plasminogen activation and is considered both a LIGAND for and a subunit of ANNEXIN A2.

An extracellular matrix protein that interacts with proteoglycan monomers to form aggregate structures. It is involved in stabilizing the interaction between the proteoglycan subunit and HYALURONIC ACID in CARTILAGE.

A DNA helicase that performs EXCISION REPAIR functions following UV damage. In humans, mutations in the ERCC5 gene can cause XERODERMA PIGMENTOSUM, COMPLEMENTATION GROUP G and increase susceptibility to SKIN CANCER.

A transcriptional coactivator protein highly expressed in SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS and CARDIOMYOCYTES. It functions as a cofactor for SERUM RESPONSE FACTOR and regulates smooth muscle contraction, smooth muscle CELL DIFFERENTIATION, and cardiac muscle development.
Amidohydrolases that catalyze the hydrolysis of endogenous amidated lipids such as OLEYLAMIDE and ANANDAMIDE to FATTY ACIDS, resulting in changes to their roles in SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION.
An RNA binding protein that binds to the HIV LONG TERMINAL REPEAT. An infected organism will produce it as RNA INTERFERENCE to prevent HIV from repressing host EIF-2 KINASE expression.
A potential-sensitive organic cation transporter protein that mediates the transport of a wide spectrum of organic CATIONS. It plays a role in the uptake of monoamine NEUROTRANSMITTER AGENTS.
giris_terimleri: Solute Carrier Family 22 (Organic Cation Transporter), Member 3

tarif: A ligand for RECEPTOR PROTEIN-TYROSINE KINASES AXL, TYRO3 and MERTK through which it regulates cell growth and survival of ENDOTHELIAL CELLS; CELL ADHESION; and CELL MIGRATION. GAS6 also has critical roles in the development of NATURAL KILLER CELLS and PLATELET ACTIVATION.
Works about graphic visual representations of educational content.
An endodeoxyribonuclease that functions as part of a DNA TOPOISOMERASE II complex to create DOUBLE-STRAND DNA BREAKS for initiating  HOMOLOGOUS RECOMBINATION  in MEIOSIS.

A cell cycle protein required for activating TUMOR SUPPRESSOR PROTEIN P53 -mediated CASPASES and APOPTOSIS. It is up-regulated during colon epithelial cell differentiation and down-regulated in COLORECTAL NEOPLASMS.
Transcription factors that play a role in the development of NEURONS. They contain a homeodomain homologous to that of the Drosophila empty spiracles head gap gene product (ems).
A homeodomain protein that plays a role in the proliferation and differentiation of HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS. It is activated by TRETINOIN.
A thrombospondin that mediates CELL-TO-CELL INTERACTION and cell - EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX interactions. It may also function as an ANGIOGENESIS INHIBITOR through its interaction with CD36 ANTIGENS.
A connexin which forms the structural component of GAP JUNCTIONS in the EYE LENS. In humans, variants in the GJA8 gene cause multiple types of CATARACT.
A homeodomain protein that influences the development and neuroprotection of DOPAMINERGIC NEURONS in the MESENCEPHALON. It is implicated in several types of cancer.
A laboratory phenomenon where a low platelet count is observed due to the action of ANTICOAGULANTS such as EDTA causing platelet AGGLUTINATION.
DNA that occurs outside of CHROMOSOMES in prokaryotic or eukaryotic cells.
A family of DNA polymerases that have the capability to carry out TRANSLESION DNA SYNTHESIS and have low replication fidelity on undamaged DNA.

A serine endopeptidase that has a similar cleavage specificity to TRYPSIN, favoring substrates with poly-basic amino acid sequences. Prostasin plays a critical role in activating EPITHELIAL SODIUM CHANNELS through cleavage of the ENAC gamma subunit.

A multienzyme complex that carries out DNA REPLICATION. Replisomes consist of DNA HELICASES; REPLICATION FACTOR C; PROLIFERATING CELL NUCLEAR ANTIGEN; DNA GYRASE; DNA TOPOISOMERASES; DNA LIGASES; and RIBONUCLEASE H.
Neuronal proteins that bind to F-ACTIN and modulate the morphology of DENDRITIC SPINES, as well as excitatory SYNAPTIC TRANSMISSION through their regulatory effects on PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE 1.
Membrane proteins which share sequence similarity with FRIZZLED RECEPTORS and participate in a variety of CELL SIGNALING activities that regulate CELL GROWTH PROCESSES and MORPHOGENESIS.
Methods that analyze the location and levels of gene expression within intact tissues.
A tyrosine kinase receptor inhibitor that targets mutants of PROTO-ONCOGENE PROTEIN KIT and PLATELET-DERIVED GROWTH FACTOR ALPHA RECEPTOR.

Evidence synthesis refers to any method that combines data and insights from multiple sources to summarize existing literature and support informed decisions, often in health, social care, or policy contexts.
Membrane and cytoskeletal-associated proteins that bind CALMODULIN and promote assembly of SPECTRIN and ACTIN FILAMENTS into MACROMOLECULAR PROTEIN COMPLEXES.
A calcium- and diacylglycerol-independent protein kinase C that protects against APOPTOSIS and functions in NF-KAPPA B signaling, CELL DIFFERENTIATION and CELL POLARITY.
Anionic polyelectrolytes that contain metal-oxo clusters. They are often used in CATALYSIS due to their structural variation and versatility.
An oxidoreductase that metabolizes 10-formyltertahydrofolate into tetrahydrofolate.

An advanced form of TUBERCULOSIS that is not being controlled by the IMMUNE SYSTEM. It requires prompt and effective treatment to prevent medical complications and transmission of the disease to other people.
A RACEMASE which catalyzes the conversion of L-Serine to D-Serine.

A thiolesterase that catalyzes the production of GLUTATHIONE and D-LACTIC ACID from the hydrolysis of S-D-lactoyl-glutathione. In vertebrates, only one gene that encodes hydroxyacylglutathione hydrolase is known to occur. In yeast and higher plants, separate genes encode the cytosolic and mitochondrial forms of this enzyme.

A technique involving a trained practitioner who places their hands on, or above a patient with the intent to guide a flow of energy into the patient. Depending upon beliefs, the goal of the procedure can include energetic healing, SPIRITUAL HEALING, or both forms of healing. While Reiki sessions may be offered on a massage table, it is distinct from MASSAGE THERAPY, which involves the physical manipulation of muscles and tissues.
An open heart surgery to treat HYPERTROPHIC CARDIOMYOPATHY.
Persons who reside in NURSING HOMES.

An extracellular matrix protein that is highly expressed in ODONTOBLASTS. It is cleaved into 2 chains: dentin sialoprotein and dentin phosphoprotein. Mutations in the human DSPP gene, which encodes dentin sialophosphoprotein, can cause DENTINOGENESIS IMPERFECTA.
Pharmacologic or non-pharmacologic methods used to improve COGNITION or AFFECT in people, especially in those who are not experiencing MENTAL DISORDERS.
Skin neoplasms that are not MELANOMA.
A non-melanoma skin neoplasm that is one of the three principal types of skin cancer. It often presents as a hard lump or ulcer and is more likely to metastasize than BASAL CELL CARCINOMA.
giris_terimleri: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Skin

tarif: An endovascular procedure to replace a diseased or damaged MITRAL VALVE.
Protein serine-threonine kinases that regulate cell growth and CELL PROLIFERATION in the HIPPO SIGNALING PATHWAY. They control mammalian cell and organ size.
